nodes.title: What actually makes it an "agent"?
nodes.one_liner: The leap from single-shot prompt to autonomous loop

nodes.title: The agent loop: observe, decide, act, repeat
nodes.one_liner: How an LLM drives iterative reasoning until done

nodes.title: Giving your LLM tools to call
nodes.one_liner: How tool/function calling works and how to define them

nodes.title: How the agent decides what to do next
nodes.one_liner: Reasoning patterns like ReAct that route each step

nodes.title: Memory: keeping context across steps

outline.rationale: The user already knows LLM basics and prompt/response wiring, so I skip all foundational LLM material and framework comparisons. The outline bridges concept to practice: node 1 defines the conceptual delta (agent vs. their current single-shot app) directly addressing their mental model gap; nodes 2-5 cover the four core mechanisms they named implicitly (loop, tools, decision-making, memory) as MECE architecture pieces they'll implement; node 6 is the payoff—building into their existing app—which is their explicit target. Nodes 7-8 cover the practical realities (control/cost, observability) that separate a demo from something shippable into a real app, which matters since they want to ship. I deliberately excluded multi-agent systems, academic taxonomies, and specific framework tutorials per the confirmed scope.
